It also relates to 'Access Transparency Consent and Control (TCC) related functions' (Type 5). While 'network connection' isn't a direct TCC category, the TCC framework aims to protect user privacy by ensuring consent for sensitive operations. If this entitlement allows an app to bypass the standard user consent mechanism (e.g., the Wi-Fi selection prompt) for joining a network, it effectively bypasses user control over a sensitive action. Furthermore, Wi-Fi connections are a primary source for location information, which is a TCC-protected resource. Automating Wi-Fi joins without consent could indirectly contribute to location tracking without explicit TCC location permissions.
